In a steady state 13C-MFA the fluxes are obtained from the fit of a 
stoichiometric isotopomer model to the measured intracellular labelling.
The isotopomer model is

* v = S · x ,   S the stoichiometric matrix of the network that is to be
analysed, and
* the labelling dynamics  dM/dt = f(v,S, M) =0 at isotopic steady state,

so that a measured isotopomer distribution Mexp fixes the flux ratios
through S. That is the whole principle of the method.

Hence in principle the method only needs

1. Metabolic reaction stoichiometry.
The topology and the stoichiometric coefficients of the reactions that
are kept in the model, including a drain for biomass formation.  Without
S there is no isotopomer mapping f(v,S,M) and no mass balance to close.

6. Isotope labelling patterns of metabolic intermediates.
The experimental isotopomer / mass isotopomer distributions of
intracellular metabolites, normally obtained by MS/MS or NMR after
steady state 13C-labelling, are the data which the isotopomer model is
fitted to.  It is the labelling data that resolves the otherwise
stoichiometrically underdetermined flux space.

The other items are not part of the 13C-MFA formulation.

2. Maximum cell density of the organism in a bioreactor
is not a model input. Absolute flux scale is obtained from measured
extracellular exchange rates / growth rate, not from the maximal
attainable density.

4. Enzyme kinetics
and
5. Regulatory networks
are not used in a stoichiometric isotopomer fit.  13C-MFA is a
topological/ steady-state mass-balance method, not a kinetic method.
Kinetic and regulatory information is irrelevant for the steady-state
isotopomer solution.

3. Biomass composition
is not strictly required for the isotopomer fitting itself.
Once S and Mexp are fixed the flux ratios and the relative fluxes are
determined up to a single scale factor.  The scale factor is normally
set by the measured extracellular fluxes / growth rate.  In practice a
closed stoichiometric model is built with a biomass formation reaction
and the biomass reaction is written with the measured macromolecular
fractions protein / lipid / carbohydrate. In that practical implementation
the biomass composition is used to define the stoichiometric biomass
drain that is part of S, and is therefore often listed as a third
practical prerequisite for a complete, mass-balanced 13C-MFA model.

That is the usual two core requirements, 1 and 6, and three if the
conventional closed biomass reaction is counted as an operational
requirement.
